inputs.assignment_instructions: Week 1 reflection (250-400 words): identify an AI tool you use, explain how you use it and what the task would be like without it; explain how the system works and its strengths and limitations with examples; state your learning goals for this course and how they connect to your career.
inputs.student_submission:
I use a navigation app almost every day. Last week I relied on it to plan a route around road construction, and it did the work in seconds by suggesting exactly what I needed. Without it I would have spent a long time doing the same thing by hand, checking several sources and probably making mistakes along the way, so the comparison is striking.

Behind the scenes, a navigation app learns patterns from very large amounts of data and predicts the most likely useful answer for my situation. Its strength is speed and consistency: it caught a problem I had missed. Its limitation is that it can be confidently wrong; once it sent me down a closed road, which showed me it does not really understand context the way a person does.

In this course I want to learn how machine learning models are trained and evaluated, and how to judge when an AI answer can be trusted. I plan to work in healthcare administration, where AI tools schedule patients and summarize records, so understanding their limits will help me use them safely and explain their output to my coworkers.

Overall, thinking about this tool made me realize how often I depend on AI without noticing it. I also talked with a classmate who uses a similar tool differently, and comparing our experiences showed me that the same system can feel helpful or frustrating depending on what you expect from it. I am curious to see how my view changes as the course goes on and I learn more about how these systems are built, tested and improved over time.
